No gentle middle step

From a free download to a 1:1 session

Someone who finds you in a hard moment can download a resource or book a session. There is very little in between for the person who wants to feel supported before they commit.

No qualifier

The people ready for 1:1 look like everyone else

The followers who would value ongoing 1:1 support read the same posts as everyone else. Nothing invites them to raise their hand.

No list engine

New clients depend on today's post

With no free class gathering emails every day, new clients mostly arrive when a post lands, and quieter weeks show up in your calendar.

The people who find comfort in your posts but aren't ready for 1:1 today have no clear next step, so most of them take none.

My recommendation

A free grief support class that offers a gentle next step and fills your 1:1 support

You already have the trust and the products. What's missing is one free 60-minute class that gives people real support, offers a small companion kit on the thank-you page, and invites the right people to apply for 1:1.

Audience + ads94.9k on Instagram, plus Meta ads to new people

Fixes the missing middle step

One free class becomes the single front door in your bio. Every sign-up is an email you keep, and every attendee feels supported before you ask for anything.

Fixes the missing qualifier

The replay page invites the people who want more to apply. You only talk to people who watched, stayed and told you what they need.

Puts your products to work

Your membership and Sisterhood in Grief stop waiting on Teachable and start being offered, gently, at the moment people are looking for them.

The 95%*

Not ready for 1:1 yet

They join the free class, pick up the companion kit on the thank-you page, and are invited to your membership and Sisterhood in Grief in the follow-up emails. They are supported, and you are paid, while trust builds.

The qualified 5%

Ready for 1:1 support

They watch to the end and apply on the replay page. The application checks fit before your calendar, and three pre-call emails help them arrive at the call feeling safe.

*The 95% / 5% split is an industry estimate, not your data.

Held: how to carry grief on the hard days, without carrying it alone

A free live class with Marie-Claude Goudreau for anyone grieving a parent, a sibling or a partner. Gentle, practical support you can lean on this week, from someone who has walked beside grieving people since 2020.

Live online · 60 minutes · Replay for 48 hours · [Date and time]

Sound familiar?

Grief doesn't follow a timeline. Neither does this class.

  • Someone you love has died: a parent, a sibling or a partner, recently or years ago.
  • The people around you have moved on, and you feel like you're supposed to as well.
  • Ordinary days, birthdays and anniversaries can catch you off guard.
  • You want support that understands loss, not advice to "stay positive".

Here's what you'll learn

Four things we'll explore together in 60 minutes

01

Grief has no deadline

Why there is no "right" way or timeline to grieve, and how to let go of the pressure to be "over it".

02

Your hard days plan

A simple plan for the days that catch you off guard: what helps, who to call, and what to let go of.

03

Staying connected

Gentle ways to keep a relationship with the person who died, through memory, ritual and words.

04

Asking for support

How to tell the people around you what you actually need, and where to find support that fits you.

Questions

Before you save your seat

Who is this class for?

Anyone grieving a parent, a sibling or a partner, whether the loss was recent or years ago.

What if I can't make it live?

The replay is available for 48 hours after the class, so you can watch when it feels right.

Does it cost anything?

No. Your seat is free, and it includes the live class, the hard days reflection sheet, a live Q&A and the replay.

Do I have to speak or turn my camera on?

No. You can simply listen. Camera on or off is always your choice.

Is this therapy?

No. It's educational grief support from a Certified Death & Grief Doula, not therapy or medical advice.

Educational content, not therapy or medical advice. If you are in crisis, please contact your local emergency services.

Script 1 · Reel · 30 to 45 seconds

"There's no deadline on grief"

Hook
"Has anyone ever asked when you'll be 'back to normal'? Let's talk about that." (to camera, soft natural light)
Body
"As a grief doula, I hear this all the time. People feel like they're grieving 'wrong' because it's taking too long. There's no timeline for loving someone who died. What helps is support for the hard days, not pressure to be over it." (slow, warm pace)
CTA
"I'm hosting a free 60-minute class called Held for anyone grieving a parent, sibling or partner. Tap Sign up to save your seat."
Script 2 · Reel · 30 seconds

"Three things that help on a hard day"

Hook
"Here are three small things I share for the days grief catches you off guard." (on-screen text: 3 things for a hard day)
Body
"One: name it. 'Today is a hard day' is enough. Two: lower the bar. Rest counts. Three: tell one person what you need, even if it's just company." (captions for each point)
CTA
"In my free class I'll walk you through building your own hard days plan. Link below."
Script 3 · Reel · 45 seconds

"Why I became a grief doula"

Hook
"People ask me what a death and grief doula actually does. Here's my honest answer." (walking, natural light)
Body
"[One line on why you began this work, in your words.] Since 2020 I've supported people through death and grief, especially after the loss of a parent, sibling or partner. Most people tell me the hardest part is feeling alone in it."
CTA
"So I'm hosting a free class called Held. It's gentle, there's a replay, and you never have to speak. Tap Sign up."
